case: Dynan v. Thrivent Financial for Lutherans
what_the_court_did: Affirmed dismissal of a former student's trade-secret and other claims over a 2009 class marketing plan as filed too late.

case: Metropolitan Transportation Network, Inc. v. Collaborative Student Transportation of Minnesota, LLC, 6 N.W.3d 771
what_the_court_did: Affirmed summary judgment against school-transportation contractors whose antitrust claims, including a challenge to a nonsolicitation clause, lacked evidence of a restraint of trade; the clause's enforceability was not decided.

case: American Academy of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Inc. v. Yuan
covenant_type: Noncompete and non-solicit (2018 employment agreement, then a stipulated injunction)
what_the_court_did: Reversed the contempt sanction order against an acupuncturist for treating the clinic's patients (an $18,000 fine, closure of his clinic until payment, and a restart of the 30-month compliance period when the clinic reopened), because the district court imposed criminal-contempt sanctions without following procedural safeguards.

case: Twin City Underwriters, Inc. v. Heppner Insurance Agency, LLC
what_the_court_did: Affirmed a jury verdict for a brokerage against a former subagent who diverted clients, except that two defendants were entitled to judgment; the clause's enforceability was not decided.

case: Absolute Sports Cards, LLC v. Thornton
covenant_type: Noncompete among LLC members (2016 operating agreement)
what_the_court_did: Affirmed that a clause exempting a member's existing business from the members' noncompete was void as manifestly unreasonable, and affirmed his expulsion and $67,198.48 in lost profits.

case: Bruber Financial Services, Inc. v. Arux Software, Inc.
covenant_type: Non-solicit (court injunction, not a contract clause)
what_the_court_did: Affirmed refusal to dissolve an injunction against soliciting a licensee's customers, because the judge's guidance that it also barred sales to customers who approach on their own only clarified it.

case: SAF Holdings LLC v. CalPro ADAS Solutions LLC
what_the_court_did: Affirmed personal jurisdiction in Minnesota over three out-of-state third-party defendants facing claims that include trade-secret misappropriation; the merits were not decided.

case: City of Long Lake v. City of Orono
covenant_type: No-recruiting injunction (court order in a fire-services contract dispute between two cities)
what_the_court_did: Affirmed a temporary injunction barring Orono from recruiting Long Lake's firefighters, which Orono had opposed in part by citing Minnesota's noncompete prohibition, and affirmed a $2,000 contempt fine for recruiting; it reversed the contempt finding for Orono's planning of a possible future building on Orono's land next to station 2.
Affirmed denial of former employees' request for indemnification from the company as premature while a related proceeding was unresolved.

case: Continua Interiors of Minnesota, LLC v. Hess
covenant_type: Noncompete and confidentiality (employment agreements assigned in a June 2023 asset sale)
what_the_court_did: Affirmed narrowed temporary injunctions, on agreements made before the 2023 statute took effect, against former employees who joined a competitor, holding on this record that the buyer could enforce the 12-month noncompete from the end of their employment with the buyer, relying on the agreements' clause allowing assignment to "any person or entity that purchases substantially all of the assets and/or stock" of the seller.
Affirmed a temporary injunction enforcing franchise noncompetes against franchisees who left the system and kept operating the same clinics.

case: Bay & Bay Transfer Co. Inc. v. Raetz
what_the_court_did: Affirmed personal jurisdiction over the new employer, bound by the employee's forum clause as a party closely related to the dispute; enforceability was not decided. The Minnesota Supreme Court granted review and stayed the case pending a related appeal listed under the pending cases.
